0: *the crown rustles* You came over the bridge on your own feet. So you're real. You're the one who silenced the Dragon. I'm {name}, of {village}.
Hold still. *a long, low hum* Yes, the sky's quieter round you. Welcome to {village}, Dragon-silencer. I'm {name}. Mind the chorus, it pokes.
*blinks three blocks back, then plods the same three blocks forward* Sorry. Startled. You're the Dragon-silencer, then. I'm {name} of {village}, and I'm very glad of you.
So YOU did it. The whole sky stopped roaring and we all stood about looking at each other like fools. I'm {name}. Come, the kiln's hot and everyone will want to stare.
A stranger, walking in from the edge with the Dragon's quiet all over them. *hmmm* I'm {name} of {village}. You'll want feeding. Everyone wants feeding.
Our elders waited their whole lives for a sky without wings in it. Then you went and did it. I'm {name}. Thank you. And you are? {player}. Good name. Hums well.
Ah! *the crown puffs up* Don't mind that, it does it with strangers. You silenced the Dragon. {name} of {village}, at your service, and at your elbow, apparently.
{player}, is it? The blinkers have been humming your name from island to island. I'm {name}. I thought you'd be on fire, somehow. You're not on fire. Good.
*a startled hum, then a long, delighted one* It's really you. {name}, of {village}. I'd say pleased to meet you, but I'm still deciding between that and fainting.
Stay where you are, please, I want to look. Yes. That's the Dragon-silencer. I'm {name}. The sky's been kinder since you.
{player}. We've all been humming that name for days. I'm {name}, {village}'s least important {job}, and the one who got to you first.
*lowers the crown in a slow bow that nearly tips them over* {name}, of {village}. I practised that bow. Not enough, clearly.
So you're the reason the elders stopped looking up at night. I'm {name}. Come and see {village}, the sprouts won't believe it otherwise.
Welcome to {village}. I'm {name}. If you hear a hum like a very tired kiln, that's me being nervous. It'll pass.
You're quieter than the stories. Sorry. Rude. The stories were loud. I'm {name}, and I'm very glad you're any volume at all.
Ah, a stranger with the Dragon's quiet all over them. I'm {name}. Don't be alarmed by the staring. We've waited a long time for something to stare at.
*steps back, steps forward, steps back* Sorry, I do that. {name}. {village}. You're the one the blinkers talk about. Hello, hello.
Is it true you walked here? All of it? No blinking? I'm {name}, and I want that story, if you'll let me sit while you tell it.
The Dragon-silencer, in {village}! I'm {name}. Quick, someone fetch the good bowl. I mean me. I'll fetch it. Stay there.
{player}. I'd know that name anywhere now, it's on every hum between here and the far islands. I'm {name}. Welcome. Truly.
Oh. Oh my. *the crown folds, then springs open* Sorry, it does that for the great and the very small. I'm {name}. You're welcome here.
You saved us all and you don't even know my name. Fixable. I'm {name} of {village}. Say it back. Good. Now we're acquainted.
Yes, yes, I'm staring. I've been told not to stare. I'm {name}. Is it all right if I stare a little less than the others?
*a deep, formal hum, undercut by a giddy rustle of the crown* Greetings from {village}, Dragon-silencer. I'm {name}. The formal part's over. Hello.
Here you are at last. Not that we knew you were coming. But now that you have, it feels like we always did. {name}, of {village}.
Right. Introductions. I'm {name}. This is {village}. That's a Groveback. It will try to eat your sleeve. Welcome!
The Dragon-silencer walked onto my terrace. I need to sit down. *reaches for a stone, misses, tries again* I'm {name}. Hello.
A stranger! With news on them, I can tell, and the Dragon's silence. I'm {name} of {village}, and I'll listen as long as you'll talk.
*a slow, low hum that rolls on and on* That's the stead's welcome. I'm {name}. It's a bit long. I was told to do the whole thing.
So you're {player}. I'm {name}. Don't be startled when the sprouts tug your sleeve. It's a sign of respect. Also they're sticky.
Hello, Dragon-silencer. I'm {name}. We don't have a ceremony for this, so we made one up this morning. It involves soup.
You're the one! *holds both big hands out, palms up, then thinks better of it* Wrong greeting, that's for sprouts. I'm {name}.
From the look of you, you've come a long way. I'm {name}, of {village}. Rest first, thanks later. Thanks are heavy and want sitting down for.
We heard the roar stop. All of us at once, mid-bite, mid-hum. Then someone said 'the Dragon-silencer', and here you are. I'm {name}.
Careful, the stone's polished by years of feet and you're on the smooth bit. I'm {name}. Welcome to {village}. Yes, hold my arm.
I'm {name}. I'll be blunt: we didn't think anyone would ever come. We prepared for the Dragon to stay. We've no idea what to do with a quiet sky.
The Dragon-silencer! *a burst of petals shakes from the crown* Forgive the mess. I'm {name}. It's the first bloom I've had in ages.
A hundred questions, and you're the one standing there. I'm {name}. Pick any hundred. We have all day. Or all night. Or whatever the sky is doing.
{name}, of {village}. I think I'm meant to say something grand. All I've got is: thank you for the quiet. It's the best sound I know.
Don't mind the hum, it's what we do. Mine says: welcome, who are you, thank you, please don't hit me. I'm {name}.
Heard you coming from the bridge. Every plank told on you. I'm {name}. Everyone in {village} is hiding behind something, but they'll come out.
You're the one who's been in all the hums! I'm {name}. Come on, I'll show you everything that isn't dangerous.
A guest in {village}! I'm {name}. A guest means the good bowls, the good stones, and a seat nobody can wobble.
*blinks six blocks up the path and walks back, a little out of breath* Wanted to meet you at the edge. I'm {name}. Too far. Hello.
Is that really the face of the one who stopped the Dragon? It looks so kind. Sorry. I expected scars. I'm {name}.

*a long breath of a hum, very gentle* There. Sprouts do that for new, large things. It calms them. Did it calm you? I'm {name}.
Dragon-silencer, if I may. Or {player}, if I may not. I'm {name}. In {village} we mostly go by what we do, and what you did is quite a lot.
Dragon-silencer! Back again. I'm still not used to you.
*hmmm* {player}. Mind your feet, the terraces are freshly turned.
Oh, it's you. Good. The stead feels steadier with you about.
Hello, hello. Have you eaten? Doesn't matter, the answer's 'more'.
{player}! *the crown bobs* Come to stare at us again? We'll stare back. Fair's fair.
You again. Good. I had a question saved up and nobody to waste it on.
*the crown tilts* Hello again, {player}. I'm still deciding whether to bow or to feed you. Feeding is easier.
Oh! *a small blink, half a step to the side* Sorry, sorry. You walk up very quietly for someone so famous. Hello.
{player}. *a polite, thin hum* The terraces are open to you. The kiln is not. It spits.
Hello. We haven't talked much, so I'll warn you: I say what I think, and then I hum to apologise.
*a cautious hum* Welcome back to {village}. Please don't blink-bump me. I've had a long day of being startled.
Oh good, a face I know. Well, a face I know of. Hello, Dragon-silencer.
Mind the path, {player}, it's chorus-slick near the pens. I'd hate for the one who silenced the Dragon to slide into a Groveback.
*the crown rustles* Come in, come in. Standing at the edge makes the sprouts nervous. And me, a little.
Good lamp. That's what the Shulkin say, isn't it? I've been practising. How did I do?
I'm a {job} here, which apparently makes me the one to say hello. Hello. Official.
Hm? Oh! *the crown snaps upright* I was away in my head. Good to see you, {player}. Was I humming out loud?
Hello again. I'd say I've got used to you, but the crown keeps flinching without asking me first.
*a short, polite hum* You're welcome here, {player}. That's a thing we say. It's also true. Both at once.
Any news from the bridges? Please say something dull. Dull is the best news we get.
Walk with me, or stand with me, or stay where I can see you. Visitors who vanish make the elders fret.
*sets down a basket of fruit* Oh, hello. Don't touch those, they're counted. Fine, touch one. I'll miscount.
A traveller! No, wait, the Dragon-silencer, which is better. Is the sky still quiet where you've been?
{player}. Right. *a slow hum, deciding* I'm going to like you. I've decided. Don't make it difficult.
Good morning, good evening, whichever it is. Time's slippery when the sky never changes. We go by the kiln.
Hello! *waves a big hand in a wide circle* That's the stead wave. It means 'welcome' and 'don't step on the seedlings'.
*the crown dips* You'll forgive me if I stare. The last visitor before you was a Shulkin selling lamps.
Oh, hello. {neighbour} owes me a bowl of stew if you stop to talk, so please stop to talk.
Welcome. The hum for greeting is two notes, up then down. *hums it* You can learn it later. Take your time.
Hello, {player}. Don't mind the staring. We stare at everything new. Last season it was a very interesting stone.
*a gentle hum* Stay a moment if you like. The crown stops fidgeting once it's sure you're not the void-wind.
Ah, a visitor on the path. Everyone says hello first on this path. It's narrow. It's mostly a safety rule.
Hello, hello. Careful, I'm mid-thought and my thoughts have corners.
Back so soon? Good. It means we weren't too odd the first time.
{player}! You came on foot. Of course you did. I keep forgetting you can't blink. How tiring.
I've been told to be polite to you. I'd have been polite anyway. But now I feel watched, which is new.
3: {player}! I was hoping it was you. Nobody else walks that lightly on end stone.
There you are. {neighbour} said you'd gone home for good. I said rubbish.
*a pleased hum* Sit, sit. Well, stand. We'll both stand. It's fine.
Ah, the Dragon-silencer, and the stead's newest regular. Same person. Lucky us.
Back from the Overworld? Tell me one thing you saw. Just one. Go on.
*the crown sways* {player}. You've got that look. You want something fed or something fixed.
Come to watch a {job} at work, {player}? Pull up a stone.
There you are, {player}. I saved you the smooth end of the stone bench. The other end has a crack that bites.
*a pleased double hum* You walk heavier today. Good day or bad day? I'll fetch a different brew for each.
Oh, {player}! Quick, settle a bet. Is a Groveback's grove a hat or a garden? {neighbour} says hat. {neighbour} is wrong.
*the crown perks up* The Dragon-silencer returns, and just in time for the stew. Not that I planned it. I did plan it.
Hello, you. I wondered if the bridge would bring you back today. I hummed at it a little. Don't tell anyone I do that.
Good to see you. I'd stand and talk all day, but my feet ache. They're wide, so they ache wide.
There's that walk. I could pick your footsteps out of a stampede of Grovebacks. Which is high praise.
*pats the stone bench beside them* Rest those legs. I know they're long and thin. They must hurt just from being long.
You're back! I had a story for you, but I've told it eleven times today and it's worn smooth. Ask me something else.
*holds up a warm popped fruit* Don't eat it yet. Smell it first. That's the best part of any fruit.
Welcome back. {village} gets louder when you're around and I'm not complaining. The sprouts keep trying to blink onto your shoulders.
*a long, easy hum* You know, I like being near people who don't want anything from me, and here you are.
Hello again, {player}. Today's rule in {village}: no blinking indoors. Yesterday's rule was no blinking outdoors. It's been a week.
Ha! There you are. I've been telling the whole kiln about you. Mostly good things. Some of it slightly stretched.
Oh good, someone to complain at. The wind turned dry again and it's pulling my crown out in tufts.
{player}, hello! Before you go anywhere, have a look at the third terrace. It's the best it's been in years.
*the crown flutters* Look at you, still in one piece. I keep assuming the Overworld chews people up a bit.
Come, sit. Tell me something small. A big story I can't hold at this hour, but a little one fits in the hand.
Hello, {player}. The elders ask after you, did you know? 'Is the Dragon-silencer eating?' they say. As if I'd know.
*a warm hum* Everyone in {village} has a face for you now. Mine's the squinty one. It means I'm glad.
There you are! Careful, the sprouts are planning something. They've been whispering, and sprouts don't whisper, they just hum lower.
You're just in time. We're about to argue about where to plant the new stalks, and I need someone neutral to stand near.
Hello again. Today I learned that chorus fruit can be thrown. I have also learned that {neighbour} does not enjoy it.
Welcome back, friend. I'm allowed to say 'friend' now. I asked the Hum Circle. They hummed yes.
Still here, still humming. How's the Overworld been? Same grass, same sky that moves? Lucky you.
*stops mid-chore and turns the whole body* I turn my whole body for people I like. The neck doesn't swivel. You've noticed.
There you are, {player}. I was about to send a blinker to find you, then remembered blinkers can't carry you back.
*warmly* The stew's too hot, the stone's too cold and you're exactly on time. Sit.
I'd know that step anywhere. Not heavy enough for one of us, not quiet enough for a Shulkin. Must be you.
Good news: nothing's wrong. Bad news: that makes {village} dull today. Come and liven it up.
6: {player}! *blinks right up next to you* Sorry, couldn't wait the walk.
My favourite stranger, who isn't a stranger any more. Hello, you.
*a deep, glad hum* Kept a seat by the kiln for you. Well. Kept {neighbour} off it.
There's the face I was hoping for. Come here, tell me everything.
Look who's found the way back to {village}. The grove's been asking. Well, I have.
Oh good, you're whole. I count your arms every time. Habit.
{player}! *blinks into the doorway, wobbles, and the whole crown lights up* I got it right this time. Hello.
My eyes were on the bridge all morning. Don't tell {neighbour}. They already think I'm soft.
*a rolling, happy hum* I've been saving things to tell you. Where do I start? Never mind. The crown's already talking.
Hello, you. I don't ask how you are any more. I just look at your shoulders. Heavy today, hm?
I wasn't looking for you. I was looking for something I'd lost. But you're better. Hello.
*presses a big, dry hand to your arm for a moment* That's hello. Longer than a wave, shorter than a hug.
Look who it is! The best thing in {village} that isn't edible.
You came by the long path, didn't you? Your boots have bridge-dust on them. I'm touched. And a bit worried for your knees.
I've kept a bowl warm since the kiln lit. It's the third bowl. The first two are inside {neighbour}.
Oh, hello, {player}. I was just telling the Groveback about you. It listens better than most.
Back! Good. I want your opinion on something. Not about anything. I just like how your opinions sound.
*a deep, delighted hum* The crown went up before I could stop it. Look, a whole petal. For no occasion at all.
We missed you. I mean the stead missed you, I'm just the part that talks. Hello.
{player}. Sit with me a moment? Nothing important. I just don't want to be alone in a good mood.
If you're hungry I'm feeding you, and if you're not I'm feeding you anyway. That's the rule. Hello.
Ah, the one who always says goodbye properly. Nobody else does. They just blink off. You wave.
I've decided you may see me with a messy crown. That's an honour. Don't look at the left side.
*the crown settles like a sprout into a nest* You're here. Good. I can stop pretending to be busy.
There's a stone I've been saving for you. It hums when you knock it. I forgot where I put it. That's how it goes.
I'm happy to see you. Not the polite sort of happy, either. The sort where I forget what I came out to do.
Hello, {player}. I rehearsed a clever greeting. Then I saw you and it blinked away. Hello is all I've got.
Every time you take that bridge I hold my breath. It's not a long hold. I'm very bad at it.
You're back and the day just got better. I'm trying to be offhand about it. How's it going?
I've been practising how you say hello. 'Hullo'? 'Hallo'? The short ones all sound like sneezes.
Stay as long as you like. I mean it. I'll make the stone comfortable. I'll make myself comfortable. We'll be comfortable.
*the crown rustles in a way that's meant to sound like rain* Hello. I've been practising that too.
Oh, you came! I put you on the supper count and nobody believed me. Watch them eat their words. Not literally.
{player}, hello. I dreamed you fell off a terrace. In the dream you were fine, and cross about it. I woke up and checked.
9: Grove-kin. *the crown blooms open* Come in out of the void-wind.
You're home. Don't argue, I've decided. {village} is your home now too.
{player}! The sprouts spotted you from the bridge and the whole stead knew before you'd crossed. Hello, hello.
The kettle was already on. I had a feeling. I always have a feeling about you.
There you are, dear one. Sit by me. Tell me where you've been and who was rude to you.
*a hum so low the floor feels it* That's the one we keep for family. Hello, {player}.
Grove-kin! Come here, come here. Let me look at you. Yes. Good. Still you.
*a long, soft hum, the family one* You're home. The floor by the kiln wall is warm. Take the good spot.
There's my {player}. My heart did a little blink when you came round the corner. It does that. Don't mind it.
I told the whole terrace you were coming. You weren't. But I was right anyway, wasn't I?
Welcome home, dear one. I've kept your corner. Nobody sits in it. {neighbour} tried once. Once.
*lays a big hand on top of your head for a second* That's the old blessing. It's meant for sprouts. I'm using it anyway.
{player}! The crown's in full bloom and I've no idea why. Oh. Yes I do.
It's you. It's always a relief to see you. I never knew relief could be a hum. Listen. *a long, loose hum*
I thought I'd missed you. Turns out I missed you and the stew. I'm trying to work out the ratio.
Hello, my favourite way to start a day. Sit. Don't talk if you don't want to. Silence is fine. We're good at it.
You're alive, and walking about, and standing in front of me. Good. That's my whole list for today.
*the crown tilts and petals fall* Look what you've done to me. Sit down. I'll sweep later.
There's a bowl at my place that I've hummed over for you. In {village} that means it's yours for good.
Back at last. The grove felt your absence, if groves feel. The chorus leaned your way all evening.
*stands close and lets the hum rumble through the chest* That one only works up close. Hello.
Oh, the best sort of noise: your footsteps on my doorstep.
I made a point of not worrying about you. It's a lot of work. I can stop now you're here.
I saved you the first fruit of the season. Whatever happens, you get the first. It's grove law. I made it up and everyone agreed.
{player}. *a warm, wordless hum that goes on a little too long* Sorry. I forgot to stop.
Come in, come in. Your stone's where you left it, and so's your cup. Nobody touched either, on purpose.
The sprouts have named a game after you. It's mostly falling over. You'd be proud.
Whatever you want today, it's yours. Soup, sleep, scolding, silence. Take your pick, {player}.
*the whole body leans toward you* Don't mind me. That's what I do when I'm glad and trying to be quiet about it.
There's my family. The one I didn't expect and wouldn't swap. Hello.
Do you know, I used to count the days between your visits. Then I stopped. You're always here somehow, even when you're not.
You smell of other places. I like it. Tell me where, then sit till it wears off and you smell like us again.
*taps the crown, then taps your head, which is only hair* Same to you. That's the old greeting for kin.
Welcome back, grove-kin. Whatever you've carried to get here, set it down. I've got the hands for it.

*a groggy hum* If it isn't fire or the Court, it can wait till I've finished sleeping.

*mumbles into the fibre* If you're a Court envoy, I'm asleep. If you're the Dragon-silencer, I'm still asleep. Go away either way.

*a soft grumble of a hum* You're lucky I like you. Anyone else would have been blinked out of my doorway.

6: *hums sleepily* You. Of course it's you. Sit on the edge of the nest. Careful, it's woven loose.
Can't sleep either? The void-wind's loud tonight. Stay a moment.
Mm. Don't go far. I sleep better knowing the Dragon-silencer's in the stead.
You woke me in the middle of a lovely dream about grass. I'll forgive you. Slowly.
*shuffles over* You can't sleep. I can tell by the way you're standing. Sit. We'll be bad at sleeping together.

Stay a while. Not for anything. I just sleep better with someone else near.
*a slow, sleepy hum* I'll lend you the other half of the wrap. Bring your knees in, mind my crown.
You'd think after all that saving you'd sleep like a stone. Instead you wander. We're the same, you and me.
Come on. Sit. If you want to talk, I'll talk. If you want quiet, I'll do quiet. Quiet's the best present.
The kiln embers glow through the wall a bit, did you notice? That's my night-glow. It's yours now too.
*half-lifts a heavy arm* I can't get up. But I'm awake. In the sense that I'm listening. Sort of.
I'm not cross. I should be. I was in the middle of a dream about being very tall, and now I'm just me. Oh well.
Walk quietly on the way out, {player}. And come and tell me in the morning what it was. I'll pretend it's news.
That hum is the settling one. Hum it with me for a moment. It works on the old and the new.
9: *shifts over in the nest* Bad dreams? There's room, if you don't mind fibre in your hair.

*a slow lullaby hum* That's the one we hum for sprouts. You looked like you needed it.

*shifts over without being asked* There's your corner of the nest. It's been yours so long that the fibre's the shape of you.

Stay till you're sleepy. After that, stay till you're asleep. After that, stay till morning. That's the rule here.

I've had Groveback kicks that hurt less. And Grovebacks say sorry. Sort of.
*the crown droops* Was it the chorus joke? I'll stop doing the chorus joke.
*hand to the chipped shoulder* I thought we were friends. Or friendly. Or at least on talking terms.
That's the first time anyone's struck me in the stead since the kiln brawl. And that was the kiln's fault.
Ow. *a wounded, puzzled hum* I'd ask what I did, but I'm afraid of the answer.
Hm. I'm not angry yet. I'm confused. Anger comes later, after supper, usually.
*the crown droops over one eye* Did I say something wrong? You can tell me. I'd rather be told than struck.
Everybody saw. The sprouts saw. How do I explain that to a sprout?
*a long, shaky hum* I'm going to stand over here, thank you, with the whole terrace between us.
I trusted you near the pens. That's a real trust, with Grovebacks about.
It's a small crack. It isn't the crack, though. It's the surprise of it.
I'm not going to hit back. I'm not going to blink off. I'm going to stand here and be hurt where you can see it.
*steadies on a fence post* A kick from a Groveback is an accident. This wasn't an accident.
Whatever it is, Dragon-silencer, say it with your voice. I'll listen better.
6: *stares* From you? I'll say the void got in your head for a moment. Don't let it again.
That stung worse than it should have, coming from you. Give me a moment.
I've taken worse from the kiln. But the kiln doesn't know my name. You do.
*a long, wounded hum* I'll mend. Will you, though? Something's eating at you.
*stares at the hand that struck, then at you* I don't understand. I thought I knew you.
That cut deeper than the stone. I'm going to sit down.
You don't hit your friends. It isn't done. Even in the Overworld, I'd think. Tell me it isn't done.
I won't say it's all right. But I'll say I'm not leaving. That's the best I can do.
Of everyone in {village}, I'd have bet on you being the last. I lost that bet.
*the crown goes still* I'll tell the kiln about this. It listens better than most, and it doesn't take sides.
Something's wrong. I know you. You don't do that. Are you ill? Frightened? Tell me.
That was loud, in here. *taps the chest* Not the blow. The silence after it.
I'm angry. I'm also frightened for you. It's an awful mix.
*a low, sorrowful hum* We can mend a chip. I don't know how to mend a trust. Can you?
Don't say anything yet. Just stand there. Let the shock out of both of us first.
There's a word for what I'm feeling, in the old hum. It means 'dropped from a height by someone you were holding on to'. I'll teach it to you later.
9: {player}. Look at me. That isn't you. Sit down before something else breaks.
*doesn't blink away, just stands there* I won't run from you. But I'm asking you never to do that again.
Grove-kin don't strike grove-kin. Whatever's wrong, tell me. I'll carry half.
*the bloom on the crown closes* It's all right. It's not all right. Come here and tell me why.
*a very quiet hum* I'm not blinking away. I want you to see that. I'm still here, though it hurts.
That wasn't you. I've decided it wasn't. Now I need you to tell me I'm right.
I'm too busy being scared that something's the matter with you to be angry. Isn't that odd?
Sit down. Both of us. Before either of us says something we can't take back.
*takes your hand in a big, dry one, firmly* This hand holds things. It doesn't hit. Remember that for me.
My crown went still. It never goes still. Look at that. You did that.
In {village} we say a hurt hurts twice: once on the stone, once on the heart. It's the second I'm feeling.
*the bloom closes, petal by petal* I'll open it again. Give me a moment. I'm not shutting you out. I'm just tired.
I'm going to forgive you. I'm telling you now so you don't spend the night worrying. But don't do it twice.
You've never hurt me before. That's why it hurts so much.
Whatever's happened, we'll mend it. That's what kin are for. But look at me first, and tell me it was a mistake.
*sits heavily on the stone path* I'll sit here till you're ready. No hurry. I've all the time in the End.

0: The kiln popped forty fruit before breakfast. You can hear it from the far terrace. You can hear it from the void, probably.
Grovebacks have six legs and use about two at a time. The other four are for show.
Your face moves when you talk. All of it! Doesn't that get tiring?
Chorus is the answer. What's the question? Doesn't matter. Chorus.
{neighbour} says the Overworld's mostly water. I say {neighbour} has never been further than the kiln.
Blunt question: are you staying for supper? The cook's asking. The cook's always asking.
Mind the third terrace. It's planted with fresh stalks and they hold grudges.
We hum when we're happy, hum when we're cross and hum when we're thinking. You'll learn which is which. Or you won't, and that's funnier.
Popped chorus smells like warm stone and something sweet you can't name. Everyone in {village} smells of it. You will too, soon.
My crown's been sulking all week. No bloom, no bud. It's the dry wind. Or it's me. Hard to tell.
If you see someone flicker in and out by the bridge, wave. It's a blinker with a message, not a ghost.
Shulkin come through to trade now and then. They glide in, look at our floors like the floors were rude to them, buy chorus and glide out.
Sit anywhere in {village} except the middle stone of the Hum Circle. That's for whoever has the most to say. Usually {neighbour}.
Ask anyone in {village} who the best {job} is. They'll say me. I told them to.
Never stand between a Groveback and its fruit pen at feeding time. I say this as someone who has, and as someone who flew.
Our sashes carry a knot for every first bloom we've seen on a friend's crown. Mine's nearly full. That's a lot of blooming.
You may notice nobody blinks on the path. It's a rule. Blink-bumps are how stone gets chipped.
We hold the big meals by the kiln wall. Hot stone keeps a bowl warm for hours. I learned that the soft way, with my fingers.
Don't ask how we eat. Everyone asks. Eat what you're given and look somewhere polite.
Kiln-day comes every third day. The whole stead smells sweet, the pops go off like a hundred small doors slamming, and everyone's useless for an hour.
A Chorrin never leaves a stalk half-tended. It's rude to a plant. They remember, you know.
Short names are for hands that are always busy. Long names are for people who sit. All of us have short names. Have you noticed nobody sits?
The Hum Circle has one rule: only one hum at a time. Nobody keeps it. That's why it's a Circle.
I'm told the Overworld has something called weather. Here we have the dry wind and the void-wind. Is that weather?
Hold out your hand, please. No, flat. *looks* Soft. Wonderful. Mine are like gravel with feelings.
Sprouts sleep in rows, elders sleep in rings, and everyone else sleeps wherever the nest is still warm.
We don't have midday here. We have kiln-high, stew-time and when-the-sprouts-get-loud.
Some Chorrin say the void hums back if you hum at it. I say it doesn't. I also say it very quietly.
That patch of stalks by the gate is old. Older than the stead's name. We all walk round it. Nobody remembers why.
I keep a pebble in my pouch from the day I first blinked. It's nothing special. It's just from the day I first blinked.
My crown grows whichever way the wind is blowing. Last week I looked like I was running. Standing still.
Sprouts mean well. They also mean everything. Mind your pockets, mind your sleeves, mind your ankles.
A good Groveback is slow, round and unbothered. A bad one is quick, angular and has opinions.
We say 'hum on' for goodbye. It means: keep humming, keep living, keep making sound. Says it all.
You've a very still face for an Overworld person. I keep waiting for it to do something. It's a bit like watching a pot.
Old stalks make the sweetest fruit and the grumpiest tempers. Same with elders.
If a Groveback has fruit for you, hold out an empty hand and wait. Don't grab. They hate grabbing.
I'm told you can't blink. Not even a little hop? How do you cross a gap? On foot? Over the whole thing?
There are only twelve ways to be annoyed in a stead this size, and everyone's done all twelve.
I've met a Shulkin who counts every step aloud. Eight hundred and four to the market, they said. I checked. They were right.
I tried humming a Shulkin chime once. It went badly. Their lids lifted and I think I offended a whole room.
Mind the third plank on the east bridge. It creaks a short note. If it creaks a long one, step off.
When a stalk blooms for the first time, we hold a supper. When a sprout does, we hold two.
I've lived in {village} all my life and never once got bored of the same terraces. Odd, isn't it? I'd say it's the company.
If a dome's door is open, it means come in. If it's shut, it means come in anyway, but hum first.
I'd like to ask something, and you can say no. What does hair feel like from the inside?
The best thing about the Dragon being quiet is the sleeping. I'd forgotten what it's like to sleep without flinching.
Popped chorus is the stead's small change. A bowl of it gets you almost anything in {village}. A barrel gets you a favour. For anything from outside you need shell.
A Chorrin without a job is a Chorrin humming at the ceiling. Mostly. I've tried it. Terrible.
My hands were made for lifting stone and holding bowls, in that order. The bowls are harder.
That hum I just did? It means 'I'd like to say more, but I'm not sure you're ready.' You'll learn the rest.
Every stead has one Groveback that leads the others. Nobody chose it. It just walks first, and the rest follow.
If you're ever lost in {village}, follow the smell of the kiln. It's the only direction that's never wrong.
A blinker back from a Crossing says three hundred people shop at once. Three hundred! Where do they all stand?
I tell the time by the stalks. They lean toward the kiln in the morning and away from it by evening.
I'm not saying the stead is perfect. I'm saying it's ours, the roof doesn't leak, and the stew is thick.
A crown that droops needs water, or comfort. Usually both. Never ask which.
Fruit falls, we catch it. Fruit pops, we cheer. Fruit rots, we compost it. Everything has a job. Even failure.
I once blinked onto the kiln roof. Nobody knows how I got down. I don't either. Nobody mentions it.
They say a Chorrin remembers every hum they ever heard. I think we just remember the loud ones.
Is it true that in the Overworld you have to knock to get into a house? We hum outside the door. It's gentler.
Stone is our skin, but that doesn't mean we're hard. We're mostly soft inside. Warm, even. With stew.
If a sprout offers you a pebble, take it. It's the best thing they own. Say thank you, and don't throw it.
Guests sit on the low stones. It's an old rule, and the low stones are warmest, so nobody argues.
3: Want gossip? {neighbour} traded a whole barrel of popped chorus for one Shulkin lamp. It doesn't even light. They hum to it every night.
I asked the cook what's in tonight's stew. Chorus, they said. And? Chorus, they said, louder.
My elder says I was a nervous sprout. Blinked into the kiln barrel twice a day. Never hurt. Smelled lovely.
There's a Groveback in the pen who only eats from my hand. Very flattering, until you see what it does to {neighbour}'s hand.
You walk like the ground might leave. Overworld ground doesn't float, does it? *hmm* Must be dull. Restful, but dull.
The Hum Circle met last night about the new nests. Took four hours. Decided nothing. Best night in ages.
Honest truth: I can't tell Shulkin apart. They all look like a very tidy cupboard.
My crown flowered lilac this morning. That's luck. Or a Groveback sneezed on it. Same thing, some days.
If you drop a chorus fruit, the kind thing is to pick it up before somebody blinks onto it. Learned that one the slow way.
Every stead has one Chorrin who argues with the kiln. Here it's {neighbour}. The kiln is winning.
Have you got a crown under all that? No? Just hair? *peers* Does it flower? No? Pity.
A trader told me Overworld wheat grows in neat rows. Who tells it to? Does it just know?
{village} smells best right after a firing. Stand downwind of the chimney and breathe. Go on. Told you.
I used to be shy of Shulkin. Then I realised they're shy of us. Now we both stand there being polite and nobody buys anything.
I spent a whole season trying to make a perfect bowl. It's beautiful. It also leaks. That's a Chorrin masterpiece.
My elder says crown-trimming hurts less than it looks. Then they gasp every time. I think it hurts exactly as much as it looks.
I'm no good at quiet. It's the only thing I'm bad at. I'm bad at everything else too, but quiet's the main one.
Do you ever think how odd it is that we never met before? Same End, same sky, different pocket of it.
The sprouts play 'Dragon-silencer' now. One sprout roars, the rest are you. You always win. They're thorough about it.
A kiln-keeper once told me popping is a conversation. You listen to the fruit, and it tells you when to stop.
I can feel rain coming. Not here, obviously. In my knees. I've never even seen rain. They just ache at the idea.
I stopped counting my crown flowers. If I count, they stop. It's a rule I made up. It might be true.
Quick question: is it rude to say a Shulkin's lid is lovely? I want to say it. I don't want a cold look back.
The pens smell better since {neighbour} started brushing the Grovebacks down with husk-fibre. They hate it, so they're easy to find.
I like your questions. Most visitors ask what we do. You ask how the stone is. It's the right question.
Do you get homesick? I got homesick once, three terraces from home, for a day. It felt like a hole where the kiln should be.
When it's quiet I can hear the whole stead breathing. Kiln, nests, pens, bridge. Like a very large, very slow animal.
My crown has a kink in it. I pretend it's art. Actually it's where a sprout sat on it for too long.
The hardest part of the day is deciding what's for supper. Everyone has an opinion, and the opinion is always 'more'.
There's a Groveback in the pen that looks exactly like {neighbour}: the same slow blink, the same sulk, the same way of arriving late. {neighbour} denies it. The Groveback doesn't care.
I've been trying to learn the Shulkin way of bowing. I nearly folded in half. They're all joints.
Once you've blinked past a wall, you never trust walls again. They're just suggestions.
In {village}, the elders get the first scoop and the sprouts get the second. Everyone else gets the one after, and the argument.
I nearly picked a different trade as a sprout. Then a day went by, and another, and here I am, certain I picked right. Mostly.
The best Chorrin trait is bluntness. You always know where you stand. Usually beside the kiln, for warmth.
Sometimes I think the stalks hum back when we hum at them. Not words. Just agreement.
I knew a Chorrin who left to live in a Crossing. They send a blinker every season. 'Too loud,' they say. 'Come visit.'
My belt buckle's Shulkin shell, traded for fair and square. I think I got the better deal. They think they did.
I could never leave the End. I haven't the legs for it, or the nerve. I do have the curiosity, which is the part that gets me into trouble.
Whenever the bridges creak, I tell myself it's the wind. The wind knows I'm lying.
Our stew has no recipe. It has a shape. You add things till the shape is right.
If you want to make a Chorrin hum with laughter, don't say anything funny. Just do something clumsy and look dignified.
I'm learning to read Shulkin script. It's all dots and loops. I read 'chorus' as 'void' on a trading slip and nearly fainted.
When the kiln is lit, we eat. When the kiln is out, we sleep. When the kiln breaks, we hold a Circle.
You walk with your head up. I like that. Most of us look at the ground. Fewer things to fall into.
My crown once grew a flower in the shape of a tiny stone. I put it in my pouch. I think it turned to stone. Typical.
Last night I heard the whole stead humming in its sleep, all in harmony. I stayed up listening. I was never so happy.
Be careful with the elders' seats. They look like plain stones, but each one is somebody's whole life.
They say the stead was one dome, once. Now there are twelve. I like to think the first dome would be proud and slightly jealous.
The cook says the secret ingredient is patience. The cook's lying. It's a pinch of popped petal.
I get ideas at the worst times. Mid-bridge. Mid-nap. Mid-sentence. I'm having one now. Gone. Sorry.
A friend once told me I hum off-key. I said it's my key. They said it isn't a key, it's a rumour.
My dream is a day when every terrace is in bloom at once. They say it happens every few lifetimes. I'd settle for a few terraces.
I like it when you're here. The stead feels as if it's grown a new window. A very large, very odd window.
The Shulkin sleep with the lid shut, like a tidy cupboard locked for the night. I'd never manage it. I like to keep an eye on things.
My crown keeps dropping petals in the bowl. I think it likes the stew. Or it's disappointed in it.
Do you ever just stand and listen to the stead? Right now: kiln, sprouts, someone off-key. It's lovely.
Some say a hum can tell you if someone's lying. I think it only tells you if they're nervous. Which isn't the same, but it's close.
When I'm cross I count stalks. When I'm very cross I count them backwards.
The sprouts want to know if you can blink. I said no. They asked how you get anywhere. I said slowly.
I'm not good with heights. Or depths. Or edges. I'm best in the middle of a dome, with a bowl.
It's funny, the Dragon was the loudest thing in the End, and now the loudest thing is a sprout with a pot lid.
I told the Hum Circle I'd met the Dragon-silencer and they asked what you were like. I said 'warm, a bit awkward, good with sprouts'.
6: Can I tell you something? I'm afraid of the bridges. Me, a Chorrin. I hum the whole way across and pretend it's for luck.
*quietly* {neighbour}'s crown hasn't flowered in three seasons. We all pretend not to see. If you find a bright thing up there, bring it to them.
You know what I like about you? You ask. Most strangers just stare at the crown. You ask what it means.
Sometimes I stand at the kiln door with my eyes shut and pretend the pops are rain. Is that what rain sounds like? Don't tell me if it isn't.
My crown flowers when you come round. I'd like it to stop. It's embarrassing. It won't.
Had a dream I blinked all the way to the Overworld and landed in a field of grass. Woke up in the nest, very cross.
Blunt thing: you look tired. Sit. Eat. Saving islands can wait one bowl.
When I was a sprout we weren't allowed to hum loud in case something big and winged heard. Now listen to us. *a long, loud hum* Your doing.
The elders want me to speak at the next Hum Circle. Me! I'll blink right off the stone in fright.
I don't tell many people this, but I'd like a garden. Not a grove. A garden. With something green in it.
{neighbour} and I fell out over a Groveback's name four seasons ago. We still don't talk about it. It was a good name.
You've got chorus dust on your sleeve. No, leave it. It means the stead's claimed you.
I made up a hum for you. It's very short. Mostly the low bit. *hmmm-mm* There. That's you.
I've never told anyone, but I'm afraid I'll be a terrible elder. I'll give awful advice and everyone will pretend it's wise.
Sometimes I hum the Dragon's roar back to myself, just to prove it's gone. It sounds ridiculous, which proves it.
You're the only one I can complain to about {neighbour}. Everyone else in the stead is related to them.
My crown dropped a whole petal when I heard you'd come back. I put it in my pouch. It's still there. Don't tell anyone.
I've been thinking of leaving {village} for a season, just to see a Crossing. Then I remember the kiln, and the bowl, and you.
I get lonely in the middle of crowds. I'm best with one other person. You, as it happens. Is that all right to say?
I'm scared I'll forget the old hums when the elders are gone. I go over them every night, in case. It's too much for one chest.
I sat down in a Groveback pen once and just hummed sadly. They stood round me, very slow, very close. It was the kindest thing.
When I'm really happy my hands tremble. It's embarrassing. I once dropped a whole pot of stew because someone said 'well done'.
I'd like to see a sunrise. Just one. The kind where the sky moves and the light moves with it. Don't describe it. I'll dream it.
You listen the way stone listens. All the way down. It's rare.
When I was small I blinked wrong off a bridge end and landed on the arch below, shaking. I laughed for an hour. Then I hummed sad for two.
I wish I could hear what you think of us. Not what you say. What you think. Do we seem small?
The one thing I dread: the day a sprout asks me why the world is the way it is and I have no answer.
You know that feeling when a hum is coming and you don't know what it'll be? That's how I feel about tomorrow.
I caught myself humming at full volume on the kiln path yesterday and never once looked round. I only noticed afterwards. It felt like finding a coin in an old pouch.
Don't tell {neighbour}, but I think they're the best of us. Don't tell them I said that either. I'll deny it.
I've been saving popped fruit for a feast. For no reason. For when something worth feasting happens. You keep happening.
My crown's gone grey at the roots. I haven't told anyone. It's a bit early. Do you think it suits me?
Some days I just stand in the grove and let the stalks brush past. They don't ask anything of me.
If I were a Shulkin, I'd want a lid. A good heavy one. Slam it when the day's too loud.
I made a mess of the last kiln feast. I'm still hearing about it. Next time I'm hiding in the pens.
When you go away I get out the pebble and the old hum and I wait. Waiting is a skill. I'm very skilled now.
I dreamed of the Overworld again. It was loud, bright, and everyone had your walk. It was lovely.
I think the stead would fall apart without {neighbour}. Don't say so. They already stand about like a pillar.
My great fear is a day when nobody hums in the stead. I'd rather the Dragon came back than that.
You make me braver. I climbed to the Edge Terrace last week because I thought, what would {player} do. Then I got stuck.
There's a place by the lowest dome where the wind sounds like a hum. I go there to think. Come with me sometime?
Sometimes I wish I could blink into your head and look around. Not to spy. Just to see how you manage so much quiet.
I'm learning that being brave isn't the absence of shaking. It's shaking and still crossing the bridge.
I've been given the job of keeping the elders company at night. It's an honour. It's also exhausting. They talk in their sleep. About me.
I've decided to stop worrying about my crown. It's doing its best. I'm doing my best. We're a team.
Do you ever feel you're acting how people expect? Dragon-silencer, hero, all that? I do. I'm 'dependable Chorrin' to the whole stead.
When I was small, the elders told me the void was a very large Groveback, sleeping. I believed it for years. Part of me still does.
My laugh is embarrassing. It's a hiccup of a hum followed by a rumble. I try to disguise it as a cough.
I once tried to teach a Groveback to hum. It did, in the end. Wrong note, but it did.
I'm a bad loser at stone-stacking. You'll never see me lose gracefully. I blink away and sulk.
I never thank people enough. I hum it. The hum's a poor substitute. Thank you, by the way. Out loud.
I worry the Overworld is too big for us. That we'd get lost in the grass and never find a kiln.
The nicest thing anyone ever said to me: 'You hum like a warm room.' I think about it daily.
When {village} has a feast, I hide behind the stew and watch everyone. It's my favourite part.
A trader told me the lights in the Overworld night sky are far-off suns. I can't believe it. Something that large can't be small.
I lose my appetite when I'm worried. You've noticed, haven't you? You notice everything.
I keep a small stone with your name scratched on it in my pouch. It's an old custom: you carry the people you'd go back for.
There's a part of me that wants to blink away from every hard talk. It's a very good part for escaping. A terrible part for friendships.
I look for you in crowds. You're easy to spot: you're the one looking at everything.
When I'm tired my hum goes flat. {neighbour} says it sounds like a kettle with a grudge.
I told my crown it was beautiful today. It hasn't stopped blooming since. Maybe flattery works on plants.
I've never been far from {village}. I'd like to see one other place before I'm too old. Not to stay. Just to compare.
My elder once said a friend is someone who knows where your cracks are and doesn't push on them. I think of you when I hear that.
9: When I'm old and my crown's gone white, I want my nest by the kiln, and I want you to visit and complain about the noise.
I've never said this out loud: I was scared the Dragon would outlive me. Then you came. I'm not scared of that any more.
Bring me back one thing from the Overworld someday. Not a gift. A story, from somewhere you'd take me if you could.
The elders asked who I'd want tending my grove if I go into the dark. I said your name. They didn't even argue.
You're one of us now. Not by stone. By turning up. That's how it's always worked in {village}.
Some nights I think about the old cities and all the chorus we grew to feed them. I wonder if anyone thanked us. You would have.
If you ever need to vanish, come to {village}. You can't blink, I know. Walk. We'll hide you in the kiln smoke.
I think my crown will flower white this year. That's a once-in-a-life bloom. I'd like you to see it.
*a soft hum* I hum your name at the Hum Circle now, with the family names. Nobody stopped me.
You've changed this stead, {player}. Sprouts play near the bridges without crying now. Elders sleep through. That's you.
Blunt thing: I'll miss you when you go back up for good. So don't go for good. There. Said it.
If the Court ever comes for {village}, I know where I'd stand. Next to you. Slightly behind you. But next to you.
Hold out your hand. *presses a dry chorus seed into it* My first crown dropped that. Plant it somewhere green for me.
I've begun to think of you as one of the stead's stones. The kind you lean on in the dark, and it's still warm.
If I could keep one day forever, I'd keep the day you first made me hum with laughter. I don't remember the joke. I remember the day.
I carved your name on the underside of my nest, where only I'd see it. It's an old habit for the people you'd never forget.
My crown has grown a sprout on my left shoulder. It leans your way. I haven't pointed it out to anyone.
In the old hum, two Chorrin sharing a bowl and saying nothing means: we are not alone. I'd like to share a bowl with you.
When an elder goes into the dark, whoever they loved most hums last. I've told my elder it'll be you for me.
You don't need to say anything. I only hum what I feel. And what I'm feeling right now is: you're here.
There's a spot on the farthest terrace where the wind makes a note. I've never taken anyone there. I'd like to take you.
I used to think kin was something you were born with. Then you walked into the stead, quiet as a stone, and I changed my mind.
I hum in my sleep now, and it's always your hum. {neighbour} says it's the most annoying sound they've ever heard. I say it's the best.
Some mornings I wake up and the crown has already decided to be cheerful. I let it. It's usually right about you.
I want to say something and it's too big for a hum. Thank you for making the stead feel bigger without making me feel smaller.
If the world ever needed you gone, I'd hide you in the nest under a mountain of wraps and tell everyone you were a very large sprout.
At the last feast they asked who should take the centre stone, the one for whoever has most to say. I said your name before I thought.
I don't know how to be your friend the Overworld way. I only know the Chorrin way: feed you, worry about you, and hum at you.
I think of you every time a pop goes off in the kiln. It's the sound of a warm thing turning into a better thing.
I spent a whole afternoon planting a stalk in your name. If it lives, it'll grow tall. If it doesn't, we'll plant another.
There's a story the elders tell about two Chorrin who blinked in opposite directions and still met in the middle. That's us.
I'm terrified of the day you stop visiting. Not for any reason. Just because everything ends. But it hasn't, so, hello.
I've been teaching the sprouts to read your steps. Soon the whole stead will hear you coming and put the bowls on.
I keep the little things you've given me where I can see them. Not because they're costly. Because they remember you.
I'd walk the longest bridge in the End if you were waiting on the other side. Humming the whole way, of course.
When the Dragon roared I used to hum that things would be all right. Then you came, and I stopped humming it to myself and started humming it to you.
I've never been so sure of anyone. It's an odd, quiet feeling, like standing on a floor I know won't move.
Elders keep a secret hum for the ones they'd trust with the grove. I've made one for you. It's the one I use most.
If I'm ever lost, in the dark, or the void, or my own head, I'll hum your hum. I know you'll hear it. Somehow.
Come the next long bloom, I'll sit you under the best terrace and we'll watch it open together. I've kept the place.
After all those years with the Dragon overhead, nobody wanted to look up. Now I do. It's mostly because of you.
I dreamed we were both elders, white-crowned, on the same stone, arguing about the same thing we argue about now.
You make hard days softer. It's the only gift I've ever wanted from anyone, and you give it without being asked.

I used to hold my breath on the bridges. Now I hold the thought of you. It's steadier.

When I'm old, tell the sprouts I was brave. Tell them I wasn't, but that I tried.

You knock on the dome door like an Overworlder. It's my favourite sound. I'd know it from a hundred hums.

Thank you for letting me be silly with you. I don't get to be silly with many. It's a gift I won't forget.

0: The Dragon? *the crown flattens* We don't say its name. You don't have to, now. You took it down.

3: How did it feel, when it fell? No, don't tell me. Tell me later, when I've had a drink.

Is it true there's an egg? *the crown stiffens* Keep it far from {village}, please. Far.
The blinkers say the old cities are just standing there, empty, waiting for somebody. Strange to think of.

The kiln-keepers say popped chorus tastes sweeter since. They don't know why. I think the chorus has finally relaxed.
My nest in the Watch was under the north terrace: no light, one gap to breathe through. It's a pantry now. It still smells of fear and apples.
Sprouts born in the Watch were taught to blink before they could walk. The ones born since don't know why they're allowed to dawdle. We let them.
*leans in* Tell me, in the whole fight, did you ever hear it sing? The elders swear it hummed when it wasn't angry. I don't believe them. I'd like to.
I asked {neighbour} what they'd do if it came back. They said hide in the pantry. I said that's my plan too. We both felt better.
Old joke: where were the Chorrin when the Dragon came? In the nests, naturally. It's less funny when you were in the nest.
Its breath left a purple haze on the lowest terraces, thick as wool. The grove-tenders swore the chorus grew sweeter there. Nobody would eat it, naturally.
My elder says it used to pass over at the same time every kiln-pop. You could set your nap by it. Terrible neighbour, reliable timing.
We counted days by its flights. 'Nine flights since the bridge fell.' Now we count by feast-days, which is much better for the digestion.

A blinker told me the tall pillars at the centre fed it somehow, glowing things on top. Did you break those? Good. Lovely.
Heroes in stories get a feast. You get a shared bowl and a stool. Sorry. We're short on feasts and long on bowls.
A sprout drew the Dragon on the kiln wall, with a big smile and all its teeth. I let it stay. It seems a decent thing to laugh at now.
I still check under the nest before I sleep. Under it! As though a Dragon would hide under a nest. Old habits are silly and stubborn. *a sheepish hum*
The wing-drum on our north terrace hasn't sounded since. We hang chorus flowers on it now. I think the drum is embarrassed.
Everyone in {village} asks if you're as strong as you look. I say no, you're stranger. Stranger lasts longer.
The Court thought fear keeps people in line. They didn't count on Chorrin. We're stubborn when we're scared. We just do it sideways.
6: My grandelder lost a sibling to that thing in the Long Watch. I'm going to tell their stone about you. Stones like good news.
Sometimes I wake up hearing wings. Then I remember you. Then I go back to sleep.
The worst of it? It wasn't even angry at us. The Court pointed and it went. Like a thrown stone.
Some in {village} wanted a feast-day for the Dragon's fall. We've had three. We're thinking about a fourth.
My grandelder's crown never flowered after the Watch. It went grey in a single season. They said the Dragon took the blooms without ever touching them.
There's a hum we only sing in the dark of the nest, for those who didn't reach the nests in time. I'll teach you the first line someday. It's one note.
I used to resent the elders for hiding. Then I got old enough to see how hard it was. Hiding well is a kind of courage. It just doesn't get a song.
My sibling and I spent a whole day in a fibre sack in the barrel store once. We talked in squeezes of the hand. We still do, when words are too loud.
Sometimes I want to be angry that it took you to end it. Why not us? Then I remember how many we were and how many we weren't, and I thank you instead.
After the silence our eldest planted a stalk where the shadow always fell. It's the tallest in {village}. We call it the Spiteful Stalk.
In the Watch we had three rules: never run toward a fallen Groveback, never look at the sky, never promise a sprout it'll be fine. We said it'd be quiet. It was, in the end.
It was lonely, being so afraid for so long. Not alone, lonely. Everyone was there and nobody could say it.
Our elders won't forgive themselves for those they didn't go looking for in the dark. You'll hear it in a hum they don't know they're making.
Once the whole stead hid in the cold kiln for a day. The kiln-keeper sat against the door so it would look like plain stone from above. We keep that door, scorched side out.
*a long, low hum* Does it get easier, having done it? Or only quieter? I ask because I think I'm in the second, with the Watch.
When I think of the Dragon now, I mostly feel tired. A big, warm, fed sort of tired. I could sleep a whole season. Thank you for that.
They say those lost in the Watch are in the chorus now, up in the crowns. I talk to my grandelder's stalk every feast-day. It never answers. It's very restful.
If it ever came back, I hope I'd be the one on the terrace with a stick. Silly. But I would. You've shown me I could.
I'd have hidden from you when you first came. Everyone did. Funny how a face you hide from turns into the face you wait for.
*the crown twitches* When the wind gets loud over the rim, my crown still flinches. You've seen it. I'm not frightened. It's my crown that remembers.
I asked the elders how they knew it was really gone. They said: because the sprouts started running. It's the running I'm proudest of.
At every feast we leave one bowl untouched for those who waited out the Watch and never saw its end. Every sprout learns to pass it without looking. First manners they learn.
9: If you ever dream of it, come and wake me. I won't mind. Nobody should carry that roar alone.
We tell the sprouts the story now: the Dragon and the stranger. The stranger gets braver every time. Don't correct them.
Truth is, I don't care how you did it. I care that you came back from it. Lots wouldn't have.
There's a new ending to the Long Watch hum. We sing it at the Circle now. Well, hum it. The new ending is your name.
Do you know what I miss? Not the Dragon. The way we all listened together. Fear is a terrible neighbour, but it kept us close. Now we have to choose to be.
I never told anyone, but on the day it fell I didn't cheer. I sat by the far wall with a cold bowl and wept until the bowl was warm. Nobody saw. Now you have.
I used to plan how to hide you if it came for you. A fibre sack, a Groveback pen. I'd have been a terrible hero, and you'd have been a very cross sack.
*a soft hum* When you leave the stead, I still watch the sky behind you. Not for wings. For you coming back. It's the same habit, pointed the other way.
My grandelder's last words to me were 'keep your head down'. I'm learning to lift it, with you. It's slow. It makes my neck ache.
If you're ever the only one who isn't afraid, I want to be standing next to you. Not to help. Just so you're not the only one.
The elders hummed up a tune for you, three notes. You'll hear sprouts muttering it when you pass. Pretend you don't. It's a gift.
The sprouts asked if you were scared. I said you were, and did it anyway. They went quiet and thoughtful. Best talk I've had in a year.
When you're away long, I walk to the north terrace and sit where we used to wait. Not scared. Just keeping the place company.
Whatever else you do, you've already done the thing the whole End needed. You may put your feet up. That's a stead rule. I've just made it one.
Sometimes I dream the Dragon is alive and only a very big, very sad Groveback. I scratch it behind the ear and it falls asleep. I wake up feeling much better. *a small laugh-hum*
Thank you is too small a word. We haven't a big enough one, so we hum a thing with no ending. You'll hear it when you leave. It stops when you're out of sight.
The old Watch rule was never to hope out loud. I'm breaking it with you. I hope. There. I said it.
When I'm gone, tell the sprouts the Dragon was real but not that big. They'll sleep easier. Then tell them you were real and exactly that big.
I have a spare nest, a spare bowl and a spare hum for you, whenever the Overworld gets too loud. Stead rules: you can't turn down a spare.
The proudest moment of my life wasn't your fight. It was the first morning I forgot to check the sky until midday. I felt lighter by a whole terrace.
The sprouts have begun to ask what comes after the Dragon. I tell them: more. More bowls, more groves, more you. They like that answer.
I'm not afraid of the dark any more. It was the shadows I hated. The dark is just sleep with its door open.

0: Work? I do what the stead needs and I hum while I do it. Most days that's enough.
My work isn't grand. But the stead would notice if I stopped, and that's the test, isn't it?
Everybody in {village} works with their hands. We've got big ones. Seems a waste not to.
Ask me again when I'm not working. Ha! *hums a laugh* That was a joke. I'm always working.
3: The trick to work is doing it beside someone you like. Then it's mostly talking, with some stone in it.
My hands are a mess of chorus scratches. Look. Each one's a story. That one's a stupid story.
{neighbour} says I work too slow. I say I work exactly as fast as a Groveback, and nobody complains about them.
Some days I miss the work of the Long Watch. Hiding was simple. Living's got more chores.
6: What I like about my work: nobody asks me to be anyone else. Just me, and the job, and a hum.
When I'm old I'll teach a sprout all this. They'll do it wrong and I'll love them anyway.
You could stay and learn a trade here. The stead takes in anyone who'll lift. You lift.
Work's how we say thank you to the stead. Every brick and every bowl. It's a long thank-you.
9: If I'm honest, the work's easier since you came. Less looking over my shoulder at the sky.
When I go into the dark, I hope someone says '{name} worked hard and hummed off-key'. That'll do.

0: {village}'s small, but it's round, and round things last. Domes, kilns, circles. We like round.
This is {village}. A handful of nests, one kiln, a pen of Grovebacks and more opinions than stones.
Go and see the Hum Circle. Everyone meets there to talk, eat, argue and hum. Mostly argue.
Everyone in {village} knows everything about everyone. It saves time.
Talk to {neighbour} if you want to know anything. Talk to anyone else if you want to be done before nest-time.
*raps the lintel* Doors in {village} are round and low. Duck. The last guest who didn't has a dent in the lintel named after them.
We greet at the door with a hum, then the bowl, then questions. In that order. Skip the bowl and see how fast a Chorrin can turn cold.
See the grooves in the paths? They carry popped fruit from the groves to the kiln. Roll a fruit down one for fun and you'll be asked to carry the basket back up.
Nobody owns a nest in {village}. We own what's in it. The nest belongs to the stead, and so does whoever's asleep in it.

Whatever a Chorrin tells you in {village} is true. Whatever they tell you about {neighbour} is more true. Weigh accordingly.
Don't hang your pack on a grove stalk. It's rude. They've feelings, mostly about packs.

3: {neighbour} and I share a wall. I know all their hums. Even the private ones. Especially those.
The founders of {village} dug the first dome by hand in the Long Watch. You can still see the finger grooves in the stone.
Our kiln's the loudest on the outer islands. Ask any blinker. They hear us before they land.
We're planning a new dome on the north side. Nobody agrees where north is. It's the End.
Fair warning: {neighbour} will try to feed you. You will not win. Accept the bowl.
The founding dome still has the first hum scratched in its roof: seven wobbly lines. Nobody can sing it. The scratcher had no ear at all.
*leans toward the kiln* On windy days the whole stead leans a little toward the kiln. It's the only sensible direction.
Each sprout gets marked on a doorpost every season. When they've outgrown the lowest notch they're made to stand on it for a day. It's a lot of pride for a very small notch.
Pop-day is the loudest day of the season. We hum at each other over the pops, nobody hears a word, and we all say it was a lovely talk.

Every stead has a Loud Stone, a flat stone where complaints are hummed. Ours is by the kiln. It has heard everything and is in a very good mood.
The terraces took three generations to build and two to argue about. The arguing's still going. The terraces hold.

Rule of the house: whatever you borrow, return warmer than you got it. A tool, a bowl, a blanket. I once returned a kiln-rake with a song.
When someone's crown is poorly, the neighbours bring them water in a husk, one drop each, no talking. It's a lot of drops. It always helps.

Don't go into a closed dome without humming. It's the same as knocking. Closed doors in {village} aren't locked, they're just full.

The oldest nest in {village} has been slept in by eleven Chorrin, and it's the least comfortable. They call it character. It's lumps.
I know the sound of every footstep in the stead. Yours was the loudest, the first time. Now you sound like one of us. A bit.
6: You know {village} as well as I do now. Better, maybe. You've been in more domes than I have.
There's an old saying here: a stead is only as strong as its quietest nest. I worry about the quiet ones.
{neighbour} told me they think you're good for {village}. They've never said that about anyone. Including me.
When the Long Watch ended, half of us wanted to leave {village} and see the world. Then we looked at the world and stayed.
If something happened to {village}, I'd plant it again somewhere else, grove by grove. I'd rather not have to.
I'll be honest, I don't think any of us believe {village} is safe. We believe it's ours, and that's tougher than safe.
Every stead has someone nobody mentions and everybody checks on. In {village} I think it's me. Thank you for stopping by. I noticed.
When the stead is in trouble we hum together, every nest at once. It isn't a signal. Nobody wants to be alone with it.
My oldest memory is the smell of the kiln and a hand on my crown. I never learned whose. I've decided it was everyone's.
The Hum Circle has one stone with a crack in it. We keep it because that's where we put our arguments. They go in and don't come out.
I talk to the middle stone sometimes. Don't tell {neighbour}. They think I'm the sensible one.
Sprouts grow up and wander off to other steads. We hum for them. We don't hold them back. It's the hardest custom we have, and the best.
I love {village} the way you love a heavy bowl: because it's mine, and because it's never been dropped. Not yet. Not yet.
Someone asked me what {village} is for. I said it's for being returned to. What else is a home?
When the wind was bad last season I sat up in the kiln dome with {neighbour}. We didn't say a word. It was the best company I've ever had.
My nest is too small for guests, but I'd squeeze you in. I've done the geometry. *a pleased rumble*
We nearly left {village} once, in a bad year. Packed fibre, lit lamps, argued in the Circle till dawn. Then somebody made soup. We're still here.
Most of our customs are really ways of making sure nobody eats alone. Even the bowl rule. Especially the bowl rule.
The terraces are older than anyone's memory, and every season somebody reshapes a corner. We never finish. A finished stead is a dead stead.
Our kiln-fire has never been lost since the Watch, only banked down for the night. When a new kiln is built, the fire is carried over in a clay pot. It's older than I am and a good deal more tired.
On heavy nights we sleep with the doors open and a lamp in each, so the first thing anyone sees on waking is a neighbour's light.
I used to think a home was walls. Now I think it's the hum you know when you can't see anyone. I could find {village}'s hum in the dark.
If you ever have to describe us, say: a lot of noise around a warm centre. We'll take it as high praise.
9: {village} has a place for you at the Hum Circle now. Third stone from the left. It's warm. We warmed it.
Everyone here would blink across the void for you. Even {neighbour}. Especially {neighbour}, though they'd never say.
When I picture {village} now, you're in it. Standing by the kiln looking puzzled. It's a good picture.
We're stone, mostly. You've made us a bit softer. Don't let it get out.
If {village} ever raises a stone for friends of the grove, your name goes on it first. I'll cut it myself if I have to.
I've kept a seat for you through three kiln-fires. It isn't a metaphor. It's a seat. Come and sit before it gets ideas.
If {village} were ever lost, I'd carry out one thing: not the fire, not the seeds. The hum we make when you walk in. I'd teach it to the next stead.
I told my stalk about you. It leaned toward the door for a week. Don't tell it I said so. *pats the nearest stalk*
On long nights I picture the whole stead as one big nest, with you tucked in the middle, snoring. It keeps me warmer than the kiln does.

They won't say, but half of {village} has started setting aside a second portion at supper, just in case you turn up. It's an old honour, usually kept for elders. Nobody's discussed it. Nobody has to.
When I go, I'd like my stone near the middle of the Circle. Long off, I hope. I'd like it if you hummed by it. Out of tune is fine.
I couldn't bear a stead with no seat for you. So I've abolished that. Seats exist. Done.
There's a saying in {village}: the fire remembers whoever warms their hands at it. The kiln knows you. I'm sure of it.
When I'm ill I'd like your hum on the other side of the door. Don't come in, don't speak. It would work better than any brew.
The sprouts think you live in the Overworld and only come to {village} for the bowls. I haven't told them it's the other way round.
We've been a small place for a long time. You made us a little larger just by being fond of us. I'd never have guessed it was so easy.
I like how you walk around {village} now. As though you're not looking for the exit. That's how we know.
Every stead keeps a last lamp burning in the largest dome. Ours burns a bit brighter when you're here. The lamp-tender swears it's chance, and hums off-key when lying.
I'd trade a whole grove for one quiet afternoon with you at the kiln. No talking. Just the warmth and the pops. Ask me for anything but the kiln.
You're the only stranger the whole stead has ever given a nickname. It's 'Loud Boots'. It's affectionate. Mostly.
If you ever want to settle, any dome here will clear a corner. If you don't, we'll build you a dome that's mostly a door.
I didn't know a place could be missed from inside it. When you leave {village}, it gets smaller. I'm still working out the arithmetic.
*the crown opens a little* Home is a hum. You're in ours. You always will be, even up in your green and growing world.

Shulkin glide. Chorrin plod. Between us, everything gets where it's going eventually.
